glosses: Originally, one's oath or word of honour, given as a condition of release from custody; now specifically, describing the release of a former prisoner under certain conditions, especially the promise of good behaviour.

examples.text: He will be on parole for nearly two more years.
He was released on parole.

glosses: Conditional release of a prisoner (now especially before the end of a custodial sentence), or the term or state of such release; the system governing such releases.

examples.text: A Minnesota woman who killed her 6-year-old son will now spend the rest of her life in prison without the possibility of parole.

glosses: A word of honor, especially given by a prisoner of war, to not engage in combat if released.

examples.text: This man had forfeited his military parole.
In hospital he gave his parole, and was enlarged after paying for the torn blanket.

glosses: A watchword or code phrase; (military) a password given only to officers, distinguished from the countersign, which is given to all guards.

examples.text: ‘Classical quotation is the parole of literary men all over the world.’
[…] their parole or watchword, which is orange, distinguishes them from the rebels in any action, to prevent disagreeable mistakes.
